title: Post-capacity event customer briefing, timeline, and remediation register
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: On 2026-02-09 22:15 UTC a capacity-related regression surfaced in us-west-2 causing sustained token-generation latency spikes and 5xx errors for ~14% of Dedicated and Hosted API requests for approximately 55 minutes. This ticket tracks the customer-facing briefing material, status page updates, and the register of actionable remediation tasks from the postmortem. The focus is clarity for customers, tracked remediation owners, and measurable acceptance criteria.
impact_summary: Affected customers: subset of Dedicated customers pinned to us-west-2 and ~3% of Hosted customers routed to overloaded pools. Visible symptoms: increased 95th/99th latency, transient KV cache misses, autoscaler thrash for certain GPU node pools. Business impact: degraded latency for production workloads, two customers observed user-facing errors and raised support cases.
detection_and_initial_response: Monitoring alert triggered at 2026-02-09T22:18:30Z (latency SLI breach). On-call engineer (Diego) paged. Mitigation path applied: temporary routing weight shift to us-east-1 and expanded burst capacity for affected Dedicated pools. Engineering notified customer success and sent an initial internal incident note. Early hypothesis: regression in kernel scheduling heuristics interacting with longer sequence workloads and KV cache evictions.
detailed_timeline:
2026-02-09 22:15 UTC - First latency spike detected by synthetic canaries.
2026-02-09 22:18 UTC - Pager triggered; Diego triaged.
2026-02-09 22:23 UTC - Temporary routing policy enacted: 20% of traffic rerouted to us-east-1; dedicated pools permitted burst.
2026-02-09 22:40 UTC - Autoscaler observed high OOM retry cycles on a node pool; engineering paused autoscaler-driven scale-down.
2026-02-09 23:05 UTC - Stabilization: 95th latency reduced to within SLO for most customers; errors decreased.
2026-02-09 23:35 UTC - Full recovery confirmed for majority of customers; monitoring continued for regressions.
2026-02-10 01:00 UTC - Post-incident sync: initial RCA hypothesis documented and shared with PM/Design/Support.
2026-02-11 - Deep-dive with serving runtime and infra teams; reproduced locally with long-prefix KV cache churn and high contention on kernel selection path.
root_cause_summary: A recent scheduler heuristic change (runtime-1.22 candidate) altered kernel selection priority for certain transformer block sizes. Under realistic long-sequence workloads this increased context-switching in the execution engine and caused KV cache eviction patterns to amplify. The increased eviction rate led to more frequent prefix recomputation, creating higher per-request token compute and triggering autoscaler oscillation in low-headroom pools.
mitigation_and_short_term_fixes: 1) Reverted the scheduler heuristic on the affected pools (rolled back runtime-1.22 candidate). 2) Applied routing policy to divert new requests away from the most impacted pools while retaining data isolation. 3) Temporarily increased reserved burst capacity for Dedicated customers to prevent autoscaler thrash. 4) Rolled immediate monitor rule to detect KV cache miss deltas and trigger early mitigation.
long_term_remediations: Tune kernel-selection heuristic with regression tests: add deterministic long-sequence tests to the CI harness (owner: Priya Rao, due: 2026-03-12)
Improve KV cache eviction strategy: add adaptive eviction threshold and soft-reservation for hot prefixes (owner: Marcus Lee, due: 2026-03-05)
Autoscaler stability improvements: introduce hysteresis and minimum cool-down for node pools with <10% spare capacity (owner: Lila Zhang, due: 2026-03-01)
Deployment gating: add performance-canary stage that runs production-like prefix churn workloads before runtime rollouts (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-03-18)
Customer SLA guardrails: add per-tenant routing weight limit and automatic fallback rules for Dedicated customers (owner: Customer Reliability, due: 2026-04-01)
Observability: add KV cache miss-rate SLOs and a combined cost/latency dashboard for early detection (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-08)

reviews_and_feedback: PM feedback (Harpreet): prefer shorter executive summary at top of public page; move technical timeline to appendix
Design feedback (Jules): suggested infographic showing routing mitigation and traffic shift to reduce cognitive load for customers
Support feedback (Clara): request for templated FAQ addressing 'is my data safe?' and 'what if we need guaranteed capacity?'
Engineering review: runtime team recommends additional stress tests before re-enabling heuristic change in any region
closure_criteria: Short-term: customer-facing postmortem published, targeted customer notifications sent, and all P0 action items assigned
Medium-term: regression tests added to CI and autoscaler hysteresis deployed to staging with soak results
Long-term: kernel-selection heuristic reintroduced only after canary validation and observed stability in production for 14 days
follow_ups: Weekly progress check-ins for the next 6 weeks on the remediation register (owner: Diego Morales)
Update Status page if timelines slip beyond committed due dates
